name: Plantoir
headline: Plan the plot. Plant your notes. Grow a class website.
tagline: Turns a folder of Markdown notes into a fast, searchable class website.
downloads_note: The download cards on the home page. A card with no 'pinned' version links GitHub's evergreen releases/latest/download/<asset>, which 404s for a platform whose installer is missing from the newest release; such a card is pinned to the last release that has it, and says so. Windows was pinned to 1.1.0 from v1.2.0, which carried the macOS DMG only, until its installer joined v1.4.2 (2026-10-03), and to 1.4.2 for the mac-first v1.4.3 cut until PlantoirSetup.exe joined v1.4.3 (2026-10-07), and to 1.4.3 for the mac-first v1.4.4 cut until PlantoirSetup.exe joined v1.4.4 (2026-10-08): pin it again in any release that lacks PlantoirSetup.exe, and unpin it in the release that ships the Windows installer again. The Mac card is pinned to 1.4.4 from the Windows-only v1.4.5 cut (2026-10-08) until Plantoir-macOS.dmg joins a later release: unpin it then. Asset names are frozen (RELEASING.md).

availability.note: On the Mac. The Windows version gets this in a later release.
availability.why: A section describing something the Windows download does not have carries {{availability:<key>}}, which prints the note while 'windows' is false and nothing once it is true. Flip the boolean in the release whose Windows installer has the feature.

new_in.why: The home page's 'New this year' list. --deploy warns when this version is not the major.minor of 'version', so a 1.5 release is reminded to rewrite it; a 1.4.x is not.

items.text: Ready-made courses for {{ready_made_ontario}} Ontario courses now, and a starting outline for about {{skeleton_codes}} more.
Deploy on a schedule, and hear how it went.
Last year's courses beside this year's, to read and borrow from.
One step to get a section ready for the first day.
A second curriculum — AP, say — with its own coverage map.
Work on a course with Claude or Codex, after telling them how you teach.
Plantoir keeps itself up to date.

redirects.why: Pages that moved, so their old addresses keep working. build.py writes each move into site/_redirects as a permanent (301) redirect, old address and everything under it, and --check refuses a move whose new page is missing, whose old page still exists, or whose old address a page still links to. 'publishing' became 'deploying' in v1.4.4 (#443): DEPLOY puts a site online, PUBLISH only marks a page. Never remove a move: outside links to the old address cannot be counted.
